area: Keystone testbed: parameter-driven enemy animation states

find.report_claim: animation_state was one of 21 Keystone modules the testbed never imported; the shooter already ships idle clips and enemy HP but had no consumer of a JSON-authored, parameter-driven AnimationStateMachine
find.live_evidence: the warden core uses StateMachineLibrary (cycle 89), a different module; the four idle clips were used for a blend space (185) and root motion (186) but never for state transitions
find.consumer_evidence: a from_dict document with calm/alert/aggressive states and three threat transitions advances deterministically: threat 0.0 stays calm, 0.5 reaches alert, 0.9 reaches aggressive

read: shooter/data/enemies.json: HP values give a 0..1 threat scalar (hp / 600)
killed: reusing the game's live state machine controller: a preview must not advance the warden core or any scene node
hardcoding the active state: the transitions and the threat parameter must be authored and exercised
letting the threat scalar come from anything but alive enemies: the preview must describe the current run
analyze.survivor: an on-demand enemy_state_preview() that builds a fresh machine from a shipped-clip document, sets the live threat, advances it and reports state plus a JSON-safe pose

fix.shooter: shooter/game.py imports AnimationStateMachine and adds enemy_state_preview(threat=None, frames=30) with three states and three transitions; tests/test_keystone_animation_state_mechanics.py (5 tests) pins authored states/transitions, threat-driven active state, JSON pose, default parameter and sim isolation; README testbed matrix and tree name the consumer and test

shooter.failing_first: all 5 new tests failed before the consumer existed (ShooterGame has no enemy_state_preview)
shooter.measured: threat 0.0 -> calm, 0.5 -> alert, 0.9 -> aggressive; report has 3 states, 3 transitions, clip warden_idle at t=0.483333 with an empty event list; default threat 0.0 with no enemies and 1.0 with a live warden
shooter.mutation: inverting the alert->aggressive operator from greater to less fails 2 of 5 tests; game.py restored byte-identically (sha256 3fb0b4835fbdaf35d2f3f293577af1e9fa350598a97871c9e77e775d4699bef9)
